claims.text: Tungsten particles will be conformally coated with a nanometer-scale nickel interlayer before spark-plasma sintering.
The nickel interlayer will reduce interfacial voids in the tungsten–copper composite.
The nickel interlayer will reduce phase separation in the tungsten–copper composite.
The nickel-coated composite will have improved thermal transport relative to a composite made from vapor-coated tungsten powder.
The nickel-coated composite will have improved mechanical durability relative to a composite made from vapor-coated tungsten powder.
Vapor-coated tungsten-powder composites typically or commonly contain interfacial voids.
Interfacial voids in the baseline impair thermal performance.
Interfacial voids in the baseline impair mechanical performance.
Spark-plasma sintering will be conducted below the melting point of copper.
The nickel interlayer acts as a reactive intermediary that enhances wetting at the tungsten–copper interface.
The nickel interlayer enhances metallurgical bonding at the tungsten–copper interface.
The nickel interlayer promotes interdiffusion between the constituents.
The nickel interlayer promotes formation of a graded intermetallic layer between tungsten and copper.
Improved wetting and metallurgical bonding during sintering reduce void formation and phase separation.
Reduced void formation and phase separation produce a more uniformly densified microstructure.
A more uniformly densified microstructure better sustains thermal transport under irradiation and thermal cycling.
A more uniformly densified microstructure better sustains mechanical integrity under irradiation and thermal cycling.
The nickel-coated composite will have significantly fewer interfacial voids than the stated baseline.
The nickel-coated composite will have higher thermal conductivity than the stated baseline.
The nickel-coated composite will have higher mechanical strength than the stated baseline.

contradictions.description: The named comparison baseline is a composite made using vapor-coated tungsten powders, but the proposed control is merely an uncoated tungsten-particle sample processed by spark-plasma sintering. Unless that control also uses the stated vapor-coating route, the experiment does not test the claimed comparison.
